title: Villagers boycott panchayat elections in Bayana over delimitation

tea.why: Residents of Nagla Singhada village protested against their removal from their original Gram Panchayat during the delimitation process.
tea.want: Villagers demanded that their village either be restored to Singhada Gram Panchayat or granted independent Gram Panchayat status.
tea.changed: Nov 3: Tehsildar Nitesh Kumar Goyal attempted to persuade residents to vote, but villagers remained firm on their boycott.

summary: Residents of Nagla Singhada village in the Bayana Panchayat Samiti of Bharatpur district boycotted the third phase of the Rajasthan panchayat elections on November 3, 2026. The protest was sparked by the village's exclusion from its original Singhada Gram Panchayat and its merger with Bangaspura Gram Panchayat, located about four kilometers away. Protesting villagers demanded that their village be returned to its previous Gram Panchayat or receive independent status. Tehsildar Nitesh Kumar Goyal visited the village upon learning of the boycott to convince residents to participate in polling, but the villagers maintained their refusal to vote.
demands: Restore the village to Singhada Gram Panchayat
response: Tehsildar Nitesh Kumar Goyal reached the village and attempted to persuade the residents to participate in the polling, but the villagers remained firm on their demands.

updates.text: Residents of Nagla Singhada village boycotted the third phase of panchayat elections over delimitation issues.
Tehsildar Nitesh Kumar Goyal visited the village to persuade residents to vote, but they remained firm on their demands.
